Dispatch SHA `7236655ef6f586169c94f3c4ce5eeccf5668960b`.
>
> Fork (b) holds. Hang 20, mint-before-Phase-4, supervisor/tee/124, and the mode pin stay. Residual #4244 and #3512 stay out. The recut-5 body cannot bind as written. This text absorbs that panel.

mechanism-shaped: true

## Why this recut

Operator-locked **fork (b)**: leave `coverage.reporter` as `["text", "text-summary"]`. No `coverage/coverage-final.json` at this SHA. Missing totals classify UNKNOWN and fail closed. Residual is [#4244](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4244). #3512 stays open; this recut does not set `COVERAGE_GOAL` to 75.

Arc 5 did not reopen json or the hatch. It did find two bind-blockers in the recut-5 text: suite-ran must be ran-vs-skipped (not an exit-0 callback), and the Phase-1 numbered-step pin is falsified by SKILL.md `:104` plus stale Step 4 pointers at `:97` and `:106`.

CI-cache diagnosis ([5573208870](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4230#issuecomment-5573208870)) was not re-run and is not refuted. RELEASING.md keeps the claimant's differential method.

## Residual (not this PR)

[#4244](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4244). Do not implement it here. Until it lands, skill/RELEASING hatch prose in this PR must not describe a live `coverage-final.json` path.

## Next-build contract — three items, one PR

**1. One suite at Step 5 (skill + pack + pin).** Delete Phase 1 numbered step 4 from the **pack** (`content/packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json`); `SKILL.md` is packs:render. In the same edit remove `task check` from Parallel prep, checklist, and anti-patterns. Write SoT is the pack; `verify:pack-drift` will fail an SKILL.md-only edit.

Move #2859 onto **pipeline** Step 5. Rewrite the Phase 1 `#2859` required-path list so no ordered-list item under `## Phase 1` invokes `task check` — today `:104` (`3. Merge; confirm task check is green`) is an ordered-list item, not prose. Sweep stale Step 4 pointers in that runbook (`:97`, `:104`, `:106`) onto pipeline Step 5. Renumber Phase 1 items 5-10. After the edit, no stale "Step 4" / `task check` ordered-list item remains under `## Phase 1`.

#4079: keep the existing mint-CLI assertion. **Delete** the `toMatch` on `4. ! Verify task check passes locally`. Pin: no ordered-list item under `## Phase 1` invokes `task check`. Do not re-anchor onto the mint sentence. Do not use a section-wide or repo-wide absence pin. Watch the "task ci:local is historical" pin (also at SKILL.md `:60`).

**2. Supervised suite-gate hang on the cached path.** New module under `packages/core/src/check/`. Orchestrator stays sync. Hygiene keeps `captureSpawn`.

- Arm the supervisor timeout **only when `options.timeoutMs` is set** (today that is `runReleaseCheck`). Ambient `task check` tees without a 20-minute kill. (`--timeout-ms` is the child flag spelling of that field.)
- Child argv comes from the resolved dispatch plan. `cliSpawnPlan` applies when `dispatch.mode === "cli"`; `ts:check-lane` is CLI-native, so the win32 `/T` walk must cover `cmd.exe` -> `deft.cmd` -> `node` as well as a direct `task.exe` child.
- Tee path: occupancy `sessionId` may be a **directory prefix only**. Filename includes a per-invocation token (pid or minted run id). Exclusive create. Two runs in the **same** session, two files. Cleanup removes only that invocation's file via `containedRemove`.
- Retention: on failure, keep the tee after named-cause readback; on green, delete after that read. Prune: sweep at **check start**, with an age bound, so a killed/interrupted run's tee is collected. Completing-run cleanup alone is not enough.
- **Named-cause:** `packages/core/src/check/named-cause.ts` already exists. Extend `extractGateCause` / `formatNamedCauseFailure`. Read the tee at the orchestrator call site and pass **strings** (do not add a path argument that pulls I/O into a pure sanitizer). Select failure-signal lines (`FAIL` or `Tests`); state a tail bound. Do not hand `extractGateCause` a raw tail (`useful[0]` would become a banner). `reason` is not raw suite bytes. Supervisor tees alone do not satisfy #3282.
- Tee writes: **forbid** per-chunk `containedWrite({mode:"append"})`. Require one contained open with a retained fd, or a justified `createWriteStream` allowlist entry (`CONTAINED_WRITES_ALLOWLIST` already has `release/build-dist.ts`). Enforcing surface is `check:framework-source` / `check:merge` (`verify-contained-writes-enforce` is **not** in `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES`).
- On deadline: win32 `taskkill /T /F /PID`; POSIX `detached: true` then `kill(-child.pid)` (not the orchestrator group). Exit **124**.
- Abnormal termination (124, signal death, supervisor kill) must remain `REAL_FAILURE` through `classifyStep5Failure` **and** must not stamp `pass_with_debt`, so the class stays closed once #4244 adds totals. Do **not** claim 137/143 currently hatch under (b) (missing totals -> UNKNOWN -> fail closed). Do not reduce to `task check failed (exit N)` before classify.
- Do not populate `failedTests` as a this-PR MUST. That plumbing belongs on #4244 if json is added.
- `classifyStep5Failure` already returns `REAL_FAILURE` on 124 / `timedOut`; `runReleaseCheck` already maps 124 to a timed-out reason. Assert, do not rebuild those.
- Release lane is **always cached** (`runReleaseCheck` does not set `noCache`). That means the cached *orchestrator* path. `ts:check-lane` is not in `TASK_REGISTRY` and is non-cacheable; a suite result is not replayed. Do not claim hang detection on both paths. Uncached `--no-cache` stays broken-but-unreachable from `task release` at this SHA.
- Keep ceiling **20** and freshness **25**. RELEASING.md: hang detection, not a success SLA; stale-binary diagnostic **before** treating 124 as a vitest hang; stop claiming the default path already enforced 20.
- Shared `.deft/release-suite-stamp.json` concurrency vs two-runs-in-one-session is **deferred** (no new stamp schema). Tee isolation is this PR; stamp provenance is not.

**3. Step 5 is a full-suite producer.** `releaseCheckEnv` (not `releaseSubprocessEnv`) sets `DEFT_CHECK_MODE=full` and **deletes** `DEFT_CHECK_AC_ONLY` and `DEFT_HYGIENE_ADVISORY`. `DEFT_CHECK_AC_ONLY` is tested **before** `DEFT_CHECK_MODE`; that delete is load-bearing. The `DEFT_HYGIENE_ADVISORY` delete is defence in depth (mode `full` returns before it is read). Poison `DEFT_CHECK_MODE`, `DEFT_CHECK_AC_ONLY`, and `DEFT_HYGIENE_ADVISORY` in `TS_LANE_POISON_ENV_KEYS` as **leak containment** for nested vitest inheriting the release pin — not a second independent stamp guard. Do not stamp unless the suite gate actually ran. No new stamp schema. Reporter stays `["text", "text-summary"]`.

Suite-ran observation:

- Invocation-local boolean, initially **false**.
- True only when `ts:check-lane` was **executed** (`CheckGateOutcome.status === "run"`), not skipped, not `SKIP_NOTICE`, not `onGateStart` / `onGateComplete(gateId, 0, false)`.
- Channel: gate outcomes already on the cached orchestrator (listed files: `cached-orchestrator.ts`, `preflight.ts`, `pipeline.ts`). Discriminator is ran-vs-skipped. Do not change `dispatchTaskCheck`'s `number` return as the required shape.
- Degraded partial skip (missing package manager) already returns **2** at `cached-orchestrator.ts:500-518`; that path does not currently stamp `pass`. The boolean can still lie if wired to the skip callback — pin it false there.
- Tests: ambient rapid env, ceremony rapid via a `ceremonyDepth` fixture (not a third env key), AC-only independently, skip/no-runner (no stamp), poisoned-input then successful full-suite (stamp allowed), and a failing suite must not yield `pass` or `pass_with_debt`. Do not reject a legitimate forced-full success.

## Docs in the same PR

Diagnostic: thresholds trigger investigation; confirm with the fresh-copy comparison (rename original, copy onto the original path); copy-over-self / reinstall. Measured 40 min -> 3.6 min on deft01 2026-09-07. Bitdefender exceptions optional (216-277 s across states, within noise).
- Release skill: one suite at Step 5; mint immediately before Phase 4 (unchanged). Pack body matches. #2859 text points at pipeline Step 5; no stale Phase-1 Step 4.
- Hatch prose in SKILL.md / RELEASING.md must not describe a live `coverage-final.json` path. Point at #4244.
- CHANGELOG entry.

- Per-chunk contained append as an allowed tee implementation.
- Occupancy `sessionId` as the tee **filename**.
- Re-anchoring #4079 onto the mint sentence, or a tautological / section-wide "Phase 1 has no suite" pin.
- Claiming hang detection on "both paths."
- Fork (a): adding `json` to `coverage.reporter` in this PR.
- Setting `COVERAGE_GOAL` to 75 (stays on #3512 / #4244).
- Treating coverage-final mtime as proof this invocation ran the suite.
- Passing raw suite bytes as the `reason` string, or a raw tee tail into `extractGateCause`.
- Populating `failedTests` as a this-PR MUST.
- Closing or recutting #3512.
- New stamp provenance schema; treating the shared stamp as isolated by tee filenames.
- Defining suite-ran as `onGateComplete` occurrence.

Poison list extended as leak containment. `coverage.reporter` is still text + text-summary.
- [ ] Residual is #4244 and is not implemented in this PR. Hatch prose does not claim a live `coverage-final.json` path.
- [ ] `task check` shows vitest-phase progress live; named-cause has this run's selected failure-signal bytes. `reason` is not raw suite bytes. Tee writes through one contained open or a named allowlist entry, not per-chunk append. Prune at check start with an age bound. `check:merge` is the contained-writes enforce surface. #3891 is not closed on 2.8 MB.

Option A / stamp provenance schema; 4h `release-publish` default and `--expires` clamp; mint-after-Step-5 pipeline seam; spawn census and #3616 (re-measure on a healthy host); WSL2; AV as a lever; hygiene-gate in-process dispatch; `vitest.config.ts` win32 `testTimeout` 240 s rationale (separate one-line PR); adding `json` to `coverage.reporter`; setting `COVERAGE_GOAL` to 75; closing #3512; #4244; #1713 B; #3482; #3479; #4215 / #4219 / #4225; Go/uv CI toolchain gates.

## Why this recut

The ~40-minute local lane that motivated this issue was **not** spawn-bound, not AV, not a platform property. It was a stale Code Integrity signature cache on two installed binaries (`node.exe`, `git.exe`) forcing full Authenticode re-validation on every launch (~500 ms each). Diagnosis chain and exclusions are in [5573208870](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4230#issuecomment-5573208870). Fix was to re-create the files. Same SHA, same host, same tree:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `git --version` (shim) | ~1,000 ms | 38–43 ms |
| `node -e 0` | ~500 ms | ~50 ms |
| `pnpm run test --coverage` | ~40 min | **216 s** |
| `ts:check-lane` (lint + build + test) | ~40 min | **3.6 min** |

16,593 tests green, coverage 88.4 / 81.6 / 93.8 / 89.4. Four further full runs across Bitdefender exception states landed at 216–277 s; the spread is within run-to-run noise on an 11-day-uptime box with a half-core of background WMI polling, so AV is an optional maintainer setting, not a lever.

With Step 5 at ~4 minutes, most of arc 2's contract is either moot or over-built. What follows is the minimum that still changes a release.

## Original (pre-recut)

## Problem

Two symptoms, one mechanism. Local `task check` on a 32-core Windows 11 maintainer box takes ~40 minutes (CI: ~4 minutes on a 4 vCPU Linux runner). A release cut runs that suite **twice** (Phase 1 step 4 `task check`, then `task release` Step 5 `task check` again), then mints a 1h `release-publish` grant *before* the second run and watches it expire before tag push (#4157, v0.111.0 on 2026-09-03).

Neither symptom is a core-count problem, and no open issue that touches this (#3482, #3479, #3616, #3891) fixes the wall clock on its own. This issue binds the actual time sinks to shipped code and names the minimal changes that remove them.

## Evidence (master `7236655`, 2026-09-06)

**The lane is spawn-bound, not CPU-bound.**
`vitest.config.ts` now records the measurement (comment landed with the #3616 `testTimeout` change): Windows process creation drains through a fixed-rate chokepoint at **~2.4–3.5 spawns/s at any concurrency** (AV filter drivers scan on execute). Serial `git --version` ≈ 400 ms; 16 concurrent ≈ 4.6 s each with flat throughput. `testTimeout` on win32 was raised 20 s → **240 s** for this reason. Repo shape today: 1,148 test files, ~16.8k tests; **122 test files spawn processes** (86 invoke `git`, 26 exec `packages/cli/dist/bin.js`), holding ~2,500 tests. `maxWorkers` on win32 = `min(12, floor(cpus × 0.25))` = 8 on 32 cores (#2546); the config's own note says lowering or raising it buys nothing because spawn throughput is concurrency-independent (#3480 / #3616).

**Gate launch overhead is serialized through the same chokepoint.**
`packages/core/src/check/cached-orchestrator.ts` (the default path for `task check`) runs the 46-entry `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` list **sequentially**, each as a fresh `task <gate> --taskfile …` spawn → `engine-invoke.cjs is-buildable-source` → `node -e` probe → `node bin.js`. ~45 hygiene gates × ~4 process starts before vitest even begins. Local `task check` does **not** use go-task's parallel `deps:`; CI `task check:merge` does, so the two paths are not the same runner.

**Lane output is captured, not streamed.**
`captureSpawn` in `cached-orchestrator.ts` uses `spawnSync` with piped stdio and `SUBPROCESS_MAX_BUFFER` (64 MB), and writes a gate's stdout/stderr only after the gate exits. The #3470 progress ticks emitted by `ts:check-lane` therefore never reach the terminal during `task check`; an idle tree at ~0% CPU and a grinding suite look identical to the operator. This is also the #3891 ENOBUFS path.

**The documented 20-minute Step 5 timeout is not enforced on the default path.**
`RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MINUTES = 20` (`release/constants.ts`); `runReleaseCheck` (`release/preflight.ts`) sets `timeoutMs` and calls `dispatchTaskCheck`, which routes to `dispatchCachedTaskCheck` whenever caching is on (the default). `cached-orchestrator.ts` never reads `timeoutMs` — the string does not occur in the file. Only the `--no-cache` path (`orchestrator.ts` `defaultSpawn`) honors it. RELEASING.md § "Vitest coverage hang recovery" describes a budget that does not exist for a normal cut; a hung vitest at 0 CPU waits indefinitely.

**The suite stamp only skips a retry, never the first cut.**
`writeSuiteStamp` has exactly one caller: `release/pipeline.ts` after its own Step 5 succeeds. A plain `task check` (Phase 1 step 4 in `content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md`) writes no stamp. On a fresh cut Step 5 always misses and the suite runs twice: ~80 minutes of gate per release on this machine before `release:e2e` (pnpm install + build + 4× `npm publish --dry-run` in a throwaway clone) is counted.

**#4157 is downstream of the duplication.**
The skill says mint `release-publish` "immediately before Phase 4"; Phase 4 then runs Step 5 (~40 min) + build + commit before the Step 10–11 closed-verb check consumes the grant. `conventions/verb-classification.json`: `release-publish` and `release-rollback` default `1h`; `release-cut` `4h`; `finish-loop` `8h`. With one suite per cut, Phase 4 is minutes and 1h suffices; the default still deserves alignment with `release-cut`.

## Next-build contract

1. **One suite per cut.** The suite stamp binds to whichever step ran the suite green at a clean HEAD. Either `task check` writes `.deft/release-suite-stamp.json` when the tree is clean and the suite passed (opt-in flag acceptable, e.g. `--stamp-suite`, wired into Phase 1 step 4 of the release skill), or Phase 1 step 4 is removed from the skill and Step 5 is the single documented run. Stamp semantics from #3187 are unchanged: dirty tree, different HEAD, corrupt stamp, or CI → miss.
2. **Forward `timeoutMs` in `dispatchCachedTaskCheck`.** The 20-minute Step 5 budget must be real on the default path; timeout maps to exit 124 and the existing `reasonLooksLikeTimeout` classification. Document that the budget applies per gate spawn (the suite gate) so a hygiene gate cannot consume it.
3. **Stream the suite gate.** For `SUITE_CHECK_GATE_IDS`, inherit stdio (or tee to a file under `.deft/`) instead of capturing; verdict and exit code are preserved. This is the #3891 fix and restores #3470 progress ticks under `task check`. Hygiene gates may keep capture.
4. **Align `release-publish` default expiry** to `release-cut` (`4h`) and print remaining validity at mint (#4157). This is the safety margin, not the fix; item 1 is the fix.
5. **Measure before partitioning.** Add a one-shot spawn census (count of `spawnSync`/`execFileSync`/`spawn` calls actually issued by a full `pnpm run test` on win32) so the #3616 partition into a spawn-heavy vitest project is sized on a number, not a file grep. Operator-side mitigations (AV process/folder exclusions for `node.exe`, `git.exe`, the repo, `%TEMP%`; running the lane under WSL2) go in RELEASING.md as *measured* options, not as the fix.
6. **Collapse hygiene-gate launch overhead** as a follow-on: dispatch CLI-native `verify:*` gates in-process from `bin.js` or parallelize independent hygiene gates. Ordering invariants from #3188 (fast before suite) and #3284 (AC first) hold.

Do **not**: lower `maxWorkers` or re-serialize files (regresses #3480; #3616 is explicit); add a silent lighter Step 5 (#2953); declare `ts:check-lane` cacheable on the source glob (#3482 stands); treat registry completeness as the wall-clock fix.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A fresh production cut at a clean HEAD runs the vitest suite exactly once across Phase 1 + `task release`; Step 5 logs `suite stamp hit` when Phase 1 ran it.
- [ ] `task release` Step 5 on the default (cached) path terminates a hung suite at 20 minutes with exit 124 and the documented remedy text; a unit test covers `timeoutMs` propagation through `dispatchCachedTaskCheck`.
- [ ] `task check` prints `ts:check-lane NN% (…files)` progress lines while the suite is running, and a 2.8 MB+ lane output never produces ENOBUFS (#3891 closes or is superseded).
- [ ] `release-publish` default expiry is `4h` in `verb-classification.json`; mint output states remaining validity (#4157 closes or is superseded).
- [ ] A spawn census number for a full win32 `pnpm run test` is recorded in this issue before any test-partition PR opens.
- [ ] RELEASING.md and the release skill describe one suite per cut and the real Step 5 budget; CONTRIBUTING iteration-lane text (#3479) is untouched.
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry.

## Out of scope

Per-file affected-test selection (#1713 B); registry completeness for unregistered gates (#3482); STEP 3 / envelope lane wording (#3479); Grok worker spawn classification and TUI (#4215, #4219, #4225); Go/uv toolchain gates in CI merge-gate.

## Root cause of the ~40-minute lane (replaces item 5 and the spawn census)

**Symptom.** Per-launch cost on this host: `node -e 0` ≈ 500 ms; `mingw64\bin\git.exe --version` ≈ 470 ms; `git --version` via the `cmd\git.exe` shim ≈ 1,000 ms (two process creations). Linux control (cloud container): 30 ms and 2.5 ms.

**Excluded, with measurements.**
- Bitdefender: AV exceptions (on-access + ATD) for the git and node binaries, the repo, and `%TEMP%` → no change. Bitdefender Shield **off** and Advanced Threat Defense **off** → no change (git 1,006–1,317 ms, node 464–577 ms).
- Smart App Control: `citool --list-policies` shows `VerifiedAndReputableDesktop` and all `…Evaluation` policies `Is Currently Enforced: false`. No CodeIntegrity operational events on launch.
- Not a uniform process-creation tax: `hostname.exe` 38–64 ms, `curl.exe` 38–72, `tar.exe` 30, `ssh.exe` 76, `true.exe` (50 KB, same Git install) 72–79, `go version` 51–62.
- No IFEO keys for `node.exe`/`git.exe`, no `AppCompatFlags\Layers` entries, no `Get-ProcessMitigation` entries. Process-creation auditing off. `AMRunningMode = SxS Passive Mode`.
- Not path-keyed: a byte-identical copy of `node.exe` at `%TEMP%\n.exe`, `%TEMP%\node.exe`, and `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node2.exe` all ran in 46–70 ms after a one-time ~260 ms first launch.
- **File-keyed:** the original renamed to `node.orig.exe` stayed 409–846 ms; a fresh copy placed at the original `node.exe` path ran 51 ms. Both carry the `$KERNEL.PURGE.ESBCACHE` extended attribute; the original's USN did not change across a launch (nothing rewrites it).

**Diagnosis.** Stale Code Integrity signature-verification cache on the two installed binaries. The kernel neither honors nor overwrites the cache entry (purge-on-write semantics; the file is never written), so every launch pays a full Authenticode re-validation — a fixed ~450–500 ms independent of file size. A fresh file gets a valid cache after its first launch. This is a per-machine condition, not a repo or platform one.

**Fix.** Replaced `node.exe` with a copy of itself; reinstalled Git for Windows (`winget upgrade Git.Git`, 2.54 → 2.55, recreates every hard-linked `git-*.exe`). After: `git --version` via shim 38–43 ms; micro-bench 102 ms/spawn serial through .NET `Process.Start` (harness overhead included), **33 spawns/s concurrent** vs the ~3/s the config comment records.

| `pnpm run test` (vitest 4.1.11, `--coverage`, 8 workers) | **216 s** |
| **ts:check-lane total** | **3.6 min** |

`Test Files 1142 passed | 6 skipped (1148)`, `Tests 16593 passed | 153 skipped (16746)`, coverage 88.43 / 81.61 / 93.82 / 89.40 vs the 75 floor. Previously ~40 min on this host; CI Linux 4 vCPU ≈ 4 min. No partition, no WSL2, no AV change, no `maxWorkers` change.

The release lane is **always** the cached path: `pipeline.ts:128` calls `runReleaseCheck(root, {}, debtIssue)` with empty seams, so `noCache`/`useTaskCache` are undefined and `orchestrator.ts:46` computes `useTaskCache = true`. Injection / swarm lens on the two pieces of shared state this recut touches.

Two things about "read this run's tee tail into `formatNamedCauseFailure` / `extractGateCause` (optional path argument)".

`formatNamedCauseFailure` (`named-cause.ts:170-181`) already takes `stdout` and `stderr` as strings. An optional *path* argument would push file I/O into a module that is currently pure sanitization and is tested as such. More consequentially: `extractGateCause` returns the **first** surviving line of what it is given (`named-cause.ts:100-104`, `useful[0]`), preferring a line that contains the gate id. `resolveProductFirstCheckMode` (`check-mode.ts:76-160`) resolves in this order: `DEFT_CHECK_AC_ONLY`, then `DEFT_CHECK_MODE`, then `DEFT_HYGIENE_ADVISORY`, then ceremony dial depth, then hard effort budget, then default full.

Deleting `DEFT_HYGIENE_ADVISORY` is **not**: with `DEFT_CHECK_MODE=full` set, the function returns at the mode branch and never reaches it -- same for the ceremony depth read and the hard-budget probe. Keep the delete as defence in depth; do not record it as load-bearing, or the next reader inherits an ordering claim that does not survive checking.

## 7. The poison-list extension is leak containment for the new pin, not a second stamp guard -- sharpens-framing

`TS_LANE_POISON_ENV_KEYS` is `[BRANCH_GATE_BYPASS_ENV, RELEASE_PREFLIGHT_ENV]` (`ts-check-lane/run-lane.ts:28`), deleted at `:60-62` before the lane spawns. ## 8. Injection / swarm lens: tee orphans and the single-path suite stamp -- sharpens-framing

The lens fires: this target adds shared state (tee files, an existing suite stamp) on a concurrent check/release path.

Tee design is right where it is specific. Per-invocation token in the filename, exclusive create, `containedRemove` of only that invocation's file, and withdrawing occupancy `sessionId`-as-filename all hold, and "two runs in the same session, two files" is the correct test.

The gap is the orphan owner. Retention says keep on failure after readback, delete on green after that read, and "state a prune rule." All three run *inside a completing invocation*. The scenario this PR exists for is the one where the invocation does not complete -- the 124 path kills the child tree, not the release process, so a supervisor kill leaves a tee that the same run then cleans, but if the release process itself dies (operator interrupt during a 20-minute hang, host reboot) nothing collects it. A prune rule that only executes on a completing run never collects the files a hang leaves behind. Name the sweep trigger -- check start is the obvious one -- and an age bound.

Second, unfenced: the suite stamp is one path per project root (`.deft/release-suite-stamp.json`), and `recordSuiteStamp` swallows every error as best-effort (`pipeline.ts`, the catch under "Stamp is best-effort"). Item 2 isolates tee filenames for two concurrent runs in one session but leaves the stamp shared. Combined with finding 1, a concurrent run that skipped the suite can leave a `pass` stamp that the other run's re-entry then hits. I classify this sharpening rather than blocking because the concurrency is pre-existing and "no new stamp schema" is a defensible scope line -- but item 2's own two-runs-in-one-session test premise is what makes it reachable, so it should be named in scope or explicitly deferred.

Stated because they were contested earlier in the arc and I re-derived them rather than inheriting them.

## Footnotes

One ambiguity worth a one-line fix on that thread, not here: under the heading "Why this is not a #4230 item," the sentence "That hole must be closed in **this** PR, not left for a later drive-by" reads at first pass as pointing at #4230's PR. It means #4244's.
- `--timeout-ms` (a child CLI flag spelling) and `options.timeoutMs` (a seam field) are used interchangeably in item 2's first bullet. Harmless once implemented, mildly confusing while reading.
- The mint sentence at `SKILL.md:180` is a lazy continuation of numbered item 2, not a separate paragraph, so the Phase 1 list is one CommonMark list of items 1-10. No action; noted because it affects how the finding-2 pin gets implemented.

## Road not taken, and steelman

I chose among three mechanisms for the suite-ran observation before writing finding 3: change the dispatcher return type (the recut's pick), reuse `onGateComplete`, or thread the suite gate's `CheckGateOutcome`.

The steelman for the recut's pick is real, and it is why finding 3 is sharpening rather than blocking. A return-type change is fail-closed by construction: every existing caller breaks at compile time and a human has to decide what the suite-ran answer is at each site. An optional callback defaults silently to "not observed," and a later refactor can drop the wiring with no test going red -- which, on a control whose entire job is to prevent a false green, is the wrong failure direction. My preference for the existing channel rests on it being already wired for every gate and already carrying `fromCache`.

What would flip me to the recut's mechanism outright: if the callback cannot be given a compile-time-mandatory shape on the release seam type. If it can -- a required field on `ReleasePreflightSeams`, or a return type that carries the outcome list rather than a bare boolean -- the cheaper channel wins. Either way the discriminator has to be ran-vs-skipped, which is finding 1 and is not negotiable in the way the mechanism is.

## Verdict

The fork-(b) lock is sound and I would not reopen it. The residual is correctly filed and correctly fenced. Items 1, 2 and 3 are the right three items, and the withdrawn list is doing real work.

Two things stop it binding exactly as written, and both are amendment-sized: item 3's suite-ran mechanism gets the wrong answer on the skip path it does not enumerate (finding 1), and item 1's pin scope is falsified by a line the recut asserts is prose, with two stale step pointers behind it (finding 2). Findings 4 through 8 change how items 2 and 3 are stated and scoped but do not stop the build.

I would not recut for findings 3 through 8.

Again a text fix, not a re-scope: the file is already listed.

## 3. `sharpens-framing` — the named channel does not reach the decision site, and the seam it must cross is missing from Files

**Evidence.** "Channel: gate outcomes already on the cached orchestrator (listed files: `cached-orchestrator.ts`, `preflight.ts`, `pipeline.ts`)." At the SHA, `gateOutcomes` is a function-local array (`cached-orchestrator.ts:167`) whose **only** exit is `RunSummaryEmitter.emitCheckInvocation({gates: gateOutcomes})` inside a fail-open try/catch (`:169-189`). It is never returned. `preflight.ts` never sees it. And the decision site consumes a **two-tuple**: `pipeline.ts:266` destructures `[ok, reason]` from `runCiFn(...)`, defaulted from `seams.runCi` (`pipeline.ts:126-128`, declared at `release/types.ts:72`), with roughly ten injection sites across `pipeline.test.ts`, `pipeline-auto-hatch.test.ts`, and `coverage-extra.test.ts`.

**Failure mode, per available option.** (a) New optional callback on `CachedCheckOptions` — legal, since it does not touch `dispatchTaskCheck`'s `number` return, but it must still cross `runReleaseCheck`'s tuple, so `runCi`'s seam shape changes; **`packages/core/src/release/types.ts` is not in the Files list**, and every seam-injected green path becomes non-stamping until updated. (b) Read the emitted run-summary back — the emitter is fail-open, so a swallowed write yields suite-ran `false` and refuses a *legitimate* green cut, which the recut explicitly forbids. (c) Module-level mutable — contradicts "invocation-local" under the two-runs-in-one-session case the tee section is built around.

**Disposition consequence.** Name the transport in one clause and add `release/types.ts` to Files. Without it, the "no new plumbing" impression the sentence gives is what gets discovered at implementation time, and (b) is the tempting wrong answer because it looks like zero signature churn.

## 4. `sharpens-framing` — the start-of-check prune can delete a live tee, and the ceiling is what makes it likely

**Evidence.** Two bullets in the same list: "Prune: sweep at **check start**, with an age bound, so a killed/interrupted run's tee is collected. Completing-run cleanup alone is not enough." and "Keep ceiling **20**." The prune is cross-invocation by construction — that is its entire purpose — while the completion cleanup is correctly scoped ("removes only that invocation's file").

**Failure mode.** Run A is legitimately hung and will be killed at minute 20; its tee is a live, growing file up to ~20 minutes old. Run B starts in the same session (the recut's own two-runs case), sweeps at check start, and any age bound below the ceiling collects A's live tee. A then reaches its deadline, exits 124, and the named-cause readback finds nothing — so the acceptance line "named-cause has this run's selected failure-signal bytes" fails exactly in the hang scenario the PR exists for, intermittently and only under concurrency. No age bound is stated, so the contract permits it.

**Disposition consequence.** State a floor: the prune age bound must exceed `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`, and the sweep must skip files whose owning pid is live. Add one test beside the existing "two concurrent runs in one session, two tees": B's start-time prune leaves A's tee intact. This binds either way — an implementer who picks a sane bound is fine — so it is a sharpening, not a blocker.

## 5. `sharpens-framing` — the allowlist escape hatch removes containment from a path built out of env input

**Evidence.** Tee writes must go through "one contained open with a retained fd, or a justified `createWriteStream` allowlist entry." The filename is derived from occupancy `sessionId` as a "directory prefix" plus a per-invocation token. `resolveRunSummarySessionId` takes `DEFT_SESSION_ID` verbatim after a `trim()` — no separator or traversal rejection (`session-id.ts:72-76`). And `verify-contained-writes-enforce` is absent from `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES`, so a raw sink is invisible to local `task check`.

**Failure mode.** On the `createWriteStream` branch, containment is bypassed by definition — `containedWrite` / `containedRemove` are the components that reject escapes, and this branch does not use them. A `DEFT_SESSION_ID` carrying a separator or `..` writes the tee outside `.deft/`, and the start-of-check prune (which the recut *does* route through `containedRemove`) then cannot collect it, so the leak is also silent. The operator sets that variable, so this is misconfiguration-shaped rather than adversarial — but it is the swarm / shared-state surface, and the one gate that would catch it does not run locally.

**Disposition consequence.** One clause: the tee path must be validated against the containment root **on both branches**, and the sessionId-derived prefix must reject separators and traversal before use. Cheap now; invisible until CI if deferred.

## 6. `sharpens-framing` — three line cites in the binding acceptance list do not resolve, and one legitimate "Step 4" is endangered

**Evidence**, from `git show 7236655:content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md` (404 lines; `## Phase 1` at `:80`, `## Phase 2` at `:195`):

- `:97` — prose, "When Step 4 (`task check`) fails…". **Correct** as cited.
- `:104` — "3. Merge; confirm `task check` is green…", an ordered-list item. **Correct** as cited.
- `:106` — **a blank line.** The stale pointer the recut is reaching for is `:105`: "4. Resume the release cut from Phase 1 (re-run Step 4)." The sweep list (`:97`, `:104`, `:106`) therefore names `:104` (already handled separately by the rewrite) and a blank line, while **missing the one residual stale pointer**. The structural pin does not save it: that pin is keyed on `task check`, and `:105` says only "Step 4". Followed literally, the #2859 recovery step keeps sending operators back to pipeline Step 4 — the tag-availability gate — instead of Step 5.
- `:182` — "7. ! **Verify the proposed `v<version>` tag is not already in use** … The release pipeline carries the deterministic gate at Step 4 (… tag-availability gate …)". This is an ordered-list item **under `## Phase 1`** whose "Step 4" is **correct** and must survive. Any pin or sweep keyed on "Step 4" rather than on `task check` will either corrupt it or fail forever. (`:203`, same correct usage, sits under Phase 2.)

**Upheld while I was there, and it strengthens the recut:** "Do not use a section-wide or repo-wide absence pin" reads as if it contradicts the adjacent "no ordered-list item under `## Phase 1` invokes `task check`". It does not — and it is **necessary**, not merely cautious. Under `## Phase 1`, `task check` also appears at `:153` (an ordinary-PR anti-pattern) and `:160` ("full Step 5 (`task check` + Vitest coverage)" — a correct Step-5 reference). A section-wide absence pin is unsatisfiable. The ordered-list scoping is doing real work; keep it and say why in one clause, so the next reader does not "simplify" it.

**Also loose in the same item:** "remove `task check` from Parallel prep, checklist, and anti-patterns." Only Parallel prep (`:87`) literally contains `task check`. The checklist line (`:89`) names no gate at all. The anti-patterns say bare `check` — at `:93` and `:379`. An implementer grepping the literal string finds one of three and leaves `:93` / `:379` still instructing operators to background `check` as Phase-1 long prep, which is false the moment this PR lands. This is author comment 5564554120 item 6, still half-open.

**Disposition consequence.** Correct `:106` to `:105` in the body and the acceptance box; add `:182` to a do-not-touch note; identify the anti-pattern lines by number (`:93`, `:379`) and the checklist by content. Numerals only — the design is unaffected, which is why this is a sharpening and not a reason to recut.

## 7. `sharpens-framing` — the RELEASING.md threshold is right in steady state and wrong single-shot (reproduced)

I reproduced the claimant's method (`Measure-Command { node -e 0 }`, `git --version`) on the endorsed host, hostname `DEFT01`, post-fix:

- First readings in a cold shell: node **96 ms** then **196 ms**; git 72 / 58 ms.
- Steady state, n=8 each: node min 69 / **median 78** / max 84 ms; git min 51 / **median 56** / max **175** ms.

This **corroborates** 5573208870 — every reading is an order of magnitude below the pre-fix 500 ms / 1,000 ms regime, so the fix holds and the diagnosis is untouched. Caveats: n=8, one host, `Measure-Command` harness overhead included. I am not offering these as a refutation of anything.

**Failure mode.** The recut prescribes: if `Measure-Command { node -e 0 }` exceeds ~100 ms or `git --version` exceeds ~150 ms, run the stale-binary diagnostic — on a **single** invocation. On a confirmedly-healthy host I measured 196 ms for node cold and 175 ms for git once in eight. Both trip the documented thresholds. So mid-incident, an operator with a genuine vitest hang runs the one-shot probe, reads a false positive, and spends the window copying `node.exe` over itself — the exact inversion the diagnostic was written to prevent.

**Mitigation already present, which is why this is a sharpening:** the recut requires confirmation via the fresh-copy comparison before acting ("thresholds trigger investigation; confirm with the fresh-copy comparison"). That second gate catches it. The one-line fix is to prescribe a repeated measurement and read the **median**, and to note that the first invocation in a fresh shell runs warm.

## 8. `footnote` — "enforcing surface is check:framework-source / check:merge"

The body pairs them; the acceptance line ("`check:merge` is the contained-writes enforce surface") is the accurate one. `verify-contained-writes-enforce` is a dep of the Taskfile `check:framework-source` target (`Taskfile.yml:478`), but `task check` dispatches through the cached orchestrator, which walks `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` — where it is absent — and never invokes the aggregate. Naming `check:framework-source` in the body invites "local `task check` will catch it." Drop it from the body; the acceptance line already says the right thing.

## 9. `footnote` — `status: "run"` is also recorded with a non-zero exit

`cached-orchestrator.ts:429-436` pushes `status: "run"` with a non-zero `exit_code` for an **advisory hygiene** failure. Harmless here, because `ts:check-lane` is not in `HYGIENE_GATE_ID_PREFIXES` (checked) — but it means `status === "run"` is not a synonym for "exited 0" globally. Whatever predicate lands must stay gate-scoped to the suite id, not written as a general "any gate with status run" helper.

---

## Road not taken

I considered treating **finding 3** as blocking alongside 1 and 2, on the reading that "Channel: gate outcomes already on the cached orchestrator" asserts an existing wire and is therefore simply false. **Steelman for the recut, which I accepted:** the sentence lists three files, which reads naturally as "these are the three files you will edit to carry it" rather than "no edit needed" — and adding an optional callback to `CachedCheckOptions` is legal under the one constraint actually stated, namely do not change `dispatchTaskCheck`'s `number` return. An implementer can bind item 3 without further operator input. So it sharpens. What tipped 1 and 2 the other way is different in kind: each contains a **stated MUST that the same recut makes unreachable** — `REAL_FAILURE` for signal death against Withdrawn `captureSpawn` signal surfacing, and "not `SKIP_NOTICE`" against a discriminator provably derived from exit 0. Neither can be closed by a competent implementer choosing well; each needs one operator sentence.

I also considered classifying **finding 6** as blocking, since `:106` sits inside a binding acceptance checkbox and resolves to a blank line. Against: the same acceptance box carries the structural requirement "no stale Step 4 / `task check` ordered-list item remains under `## Phase 1`", which does cover `:105` on a careful read. Wrong numerals cost a verification cycle; they do not stop the item from binding.

---

## Disposition

Fork (b), the residual boundary (#4244 out, #3512 untouched), ceiling 20, freshness 25, mint-before-Phase-4, the supervisor / tee / 124 shape, "cached path only", the `releaseCheckEnv` pin with the load-bearing `DEFT_CHECK_AC_ONLY` delete, the `ceremonyDepth` fixture, and the pack-as-write-SoT edit all hold under re-verification. Nothing here reopens json, the hatch, #3512, or #4244.

Two clauses stand between this text and a bindable contract: finding 1 (signal death classifies `UNKNOWN`, and say so instead of `REAL_FAILURE`) and finding 2 (suite-ran needs a lane-side execution signal, in a file already on the Files list). Both are additions to existing bullets. Findings 3-7 are in-flight corrections: one transport clause plus `release/types.ts` in Files; a prune age-bound floor above the ceiling; path validation on the allowlist branch; `:106` to `:105` with `:182` protected and the anti-pattern lines named; and a median-of-N in the RELEASING.md probe.
